subject: Franska 4
title: Idiomatic expressions and false friends
sourceSummary: Common French idioms that can't be translated word for word, plus classic false friends between French and Swedish that easily cause misunderstandings.

questions.prompt: What does the expression "poser un lapin à quelqu'un" mean?
questions.opener: Literally "to put a rabbit on someone" — but it's not about animals.
choices: To cheat someone out of money
To stand someone up for an arranged meeting
To give someone a last-minute gift
questions.explanation: "Poser un lapin à quelqu'un" means to stand someone up, i.e. not show up to an arranged meeting without warning: "Il m'a posé un lapin hier soir" (he stood me up last night).

questions.prompt: What does the French word "actuellement" mean?
questions.opener: A classic trap — the word looks like the Swedish "aktuellt", but it means something else.
questions.explanation: "Actuellement" is a false friend — it means "currently/at present", not "aktuellt" (topical). "Current/relevant" in the sense of "present-day" is "actuel", but for "what's in the news right now" you'd rather use "d'actualité". "In fact/actually" is "en fait" in French.

questions.prompt: If a French speaker says "Je vais à la librairie", where are they headed?
questions.opener: "Librairie" looks like the Swedish word for "library", but it means something else.
questions.explanation: "Librairie" means bookshop, not library — it's a classic false friend. "Library" is "bibliothèque" in French.

questions.opener: The word looks exactly like the English "sensible", but French tricks you here.
questions.explanation: "Sensible" in French means sensitive/easily moved, not "reasonable" as in English. "Reasonable" is instead "raisonnable" or "sensé" in French — a treacherous pair for anyone who also speaks English.

questions.opener: Literally "to have the cockroach" — a casual expression for a mood.
choices: To be in a bad mood, down
To be stressed about a test
questions.explanation: "Avoir le cafard" is a casual expression meaning to feel down or blue: "J'ai un peu le cafard aujourd'hui" (I'm feeling a bit down today).

questions.prompt: In what context would you say "Ça marche !" in everyday French?
questions.opener: Picture someone proposing a plan and you agreeing to it.
choices: When describing that a machine is working
As an agreeing reply to a suggestion, meaning "okay, that works!"
When talking about going for a walk
questions.explanation: "Ça marche !" is used colloquially as an agreeing reply to a suggestion, roughly "that works!" or "okay, deal!" — in addition to its literal meaning that something is working or functioning.

questions.prompt: Correct the errors in this text, written by a student who mixed up false friends: "Actuellement, je lis un roman très intéressant, mais mon frère est très sensible aux critiques quand je lui en parle."
questions.opener: Read the sentence and ask yourself whether each suspicious-looking word really means what the student thought.
questions.answer: The sentence is actually already correct — but explain why the words don't mean what you might assume.
steps: "Actuellement" here correctly means "currently" — so the student has used the word correctly, even though it looks like the Swedish word for "topical". The sentence "actuellement, je lis un roman" means "right now I'm reading a novel", which is accurate.

"Sensible" is also used correctly here in the sense of "sensitive, easily moved": "mon frère est très sensible aux critiques" means "my brother is very sensitive to criticism" — exactly what is being described.

The point of the exercise: these two words LOOK like Swedish/English words with a different meaning, but here they are used with their correct French meaning. The trap is BELIEVING they mean the same as in Swedish/English and therefore misusing them in a different sentence.

If the student had instead wanted to say "my brother is reasonable", "sensible" would have been the wrong choice — "raisonnable" is needed there. And if the student had wanted to say "it's topical/relevant right now", "actuellement" wouldn't work — "d'actualité" is needed there.

questions.prompt: What are the most common French-Swedish false friends to watch out for, and what do they actually mean?
questions.opener: A list worth reviewing before reading comprehension and writing tasks.
questions.answer: actuellement = currently (NOT topical → d'actualité) · librairie = bookshop (NOT library → bibliothèque) · sensible = sensitive (NOT reasonable → raisonnable/sensé) · demander = to ask/ask for (NOT to demand → exiger) · attendre = to wait (NOT to attend → assister à) · assister à = to attend/be present at (NOT to assist → aider) · une chance = a stroke of luck/opportunity (can mean luck, not just "chance" in the sense of risk) · rester = to stay/remain (NOT to travel → voyager) · un préservatif = a condom (NOT a preservative → un conservateur). Idioms worth knowing: poser un lapin (to stand someone up), avoir le cafard (to feel down), Ça marche ! (that works/okay!).
